title: EXP-071-R2 - Hello World Part 4 Section 11a: Create the FX_Orders SQL Table and IDO with the Maintenance Wizard (replay: visible absence criteria)
objective: Replay of EXP-071, which stopped at the collision gate because neither FX_Orders absence query had a visible criterion (zero rows, but no capture of the typed criterion; the IDOs criteria field became read-only after the query). Nothing was created. The positive controls (FX_Items, dbo.FX_Items) and the dependency gate passed in EXP-071 and carry over. Follow hello-world-pt4.md Section 11 steps 1-4 (14:56-15:50), adapted to FX_ names, with the Web Designer New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance wizard as in EXP-049. Prove the IDO FX_Orders and the SQL table dbo.FX_Orders absent and the dependencies available, then create them in one wizard run in FX_HelloWorldProject01 with Table Alias fxords and exactly four properties in order: FX_OrderNumber (Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key, Required); FX_CustomerID (Property Class FX_CustomerID, Required); FX_Item (Property Class FX_Item, Length overridden to 50, Required); FX_Count (Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount, Default Value 1). The wizard Property Class lookup must list FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item; only if a class is missing, one Designer metadata unload (operator-authorized for this experiment) is allowed before one re-check. Verify the configuration, invoke Finish once, and answer No to the Create Form prompt (the FX_Orders Form follows in EXP-072). Check in the new FX_Orders IDO once if it is left checked out. Close and reopen the IDOs and SQL Tables Forms once each and recover both objects. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt4.md Section 11 (14:56-16:34) and its Orders schema quick reference, the EXP-071 record and final report (gate failure, read-only criteria field), the EXP-049 record (wizard route, read-only Table Name, grid-editor intercepts, check-in, SQL Columns verification) and the EXP-070 record (the three property classes) before browser interaction; read EXP-044 only as needed.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-071-R2-hello-world-part-4-section-11a-fx-orders-table-and-ido.md and evidence/EXP-071-R2/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection.

Collision gate: the IDOs and Sql Tables Forms are open from EXP-071 (Filter in Place, Save disabled; Sql Tables shows an unsaved add-mode placeholder row). If each is clean, close it once through its Form-tab control and reopen it once through Form > Open > Select Form. In each fresh Form: enter Filter in Place once, verify the name criteria field is editable, type the exact name (FX_Orders in the IDOs IDO Name; FX_Orders in the Sql Tables Table Name) and commit with Tab, take a screenshot showing the criterion before F4, press F4 once, and take a screenshot of the settled result. Absence is established only by zero data rows with the criterion visible before F4. If a Form is not clean, a criteria field is read-only, or a result is ambiguous, stop blocked. The EXP-071 positive controls (t1-07 FX_Items, t1-10 dbo.FX_Items) carry over.
Dependency gate: carried over from EXP-071 T1 (AC-2 passed: t1-00, t1-01, t1-03, t1-05). Re-read nothing unless the session shows a change.

Wizard: in the Web Designer open New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance once (EXP-049 route); set IDO Name FX_Orders, IDO Project FX_HelloWorldProject01 and Table Alias fxords. With Site Split unchecked the Table Name is read-only and empty and derived from the IDO name on Finish (EXP-049); do not type into it.

Properties, in order: FX_OrderNumber with Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key and Required; FX_CustomerID with Property Class FX_CustomerID and Required; FX_Item with Property Class FX_Item, Length 50 and Required; FX_Count with Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount and Default Value 1. Use the native Property Class lookup and commit typed values with Tab; record each resolved inherited value and any SQL Column Data Type the wizard shows or requires (the tutorial sets one for Customer ID; FX_CustomerID already supplies nvarchar).

Grid editors (EXP-049 rule): per cell, one editor-intercepted timeout is allowed; take one fresh snapshot and continue with the now-active editor of the target cell. A second intercept on the same cell, an unexpected value or any other timeout is a stop.

Lookup contingency: only if the Property Class lookup does not list one of FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item, record the visible list, invoke the Web Designer Unload All Global Form Objects once (Designer clean, wizard closed with its native Cancel first), reopen the wizard once and re-check; if a class is still missing, stop blocked.
Verify all four rows, their order, values, classes and key and required flags before Finish; invoke Finish once and record the completion message; answer No once to the Create Form prompt.

Inspect FX_Orders in the IDOs Form (project, table, alias, the four properties with their classes, effective values and the Count default) and dbo.FX_Orders in SQL Tables / SQL Columns (business column types, lengths, nullability, primary key, system columns distinguished).
If FX_Orders is visibly checked out after creation, perform exactly one native check-in of FX_Orders only and record the result; otherwise perform none.

After creation and clean states, close and reopen the IDOs Form once more and the Sql Tables Form once more (the recovery pair, in addition to the pre-gate pair); recover each object with one fresh exact-name query and compare with the post-creation readbacks.

Capture screenshots of the gates, the wizard header, each configured property row, the four-row grid before Finish, the completion and Create Form prompts, the IDO and SQL readbacks, any check-in and the recoveries.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.
out_of_scope: Creating the FX_Orders Form (EXP-072) or any other Form, and editing existing Forms.
Changing any property class, existing IDO, table, project, string, extension or theme; creating the FX_sCount string or other strings.
Any unload other than the single lookup-contingency Designer unload; any Web Client unload, FormSync, deployment or regeneration.
Checkout-management actions other than the single conditional check-in of the new FX_Orders IDO.
Creating records in FX_Orders or editing any runtime records.
Browser JavaScript, console or network inspection, direct URL navigation (except the portal step of the session-expiry procedure), refresh or restart.
Modifying earlier experiment records, AGENTS.md, tutorial sources, recipes or files outside the EXP-071-R2 paths.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Never proceed if FX_Orders or dbo.FX_Orders already exists, a gate is ambiguous, or a dependency is missing.
Never modify a property class, an existing IDO or table, FX_HelloWorldProject01 or any string.
Never invoke Finish before all four properties are verified, more than once, or retry an ambiguous Finish; never recreate a partial object.
Never accept the Create Form prompt; answer No once.
Never invoke more than one Unload All Global Form Objects, never one in the Web Client, and never one unless a required class is missing from the lookup.
Never perform a checkout-management action other than the single conditional check-in of FX_Orders.
Never repair, rename or remove a partial SQL or IDO artifact if blocked; stop and report.
Never close a dirty Form or discard changes without operator approval.
Never click the Designer top-toolbar Delete button (Delete Form Definition).
Never use direct SQL, scripts, application internals or browser JavaScript.
Never refresh, restart or replace the browser session; re-login only through the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure, at most once per task.
Never run more than one recovery query per object after its recovery reopen, or more than two closes and two reopens per Form (one pre-gate pair and one recovery pair).
Never claim database durability or replay verification from same-session UI recovery.

target.form: New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance wizard

acceptance_checks.description: Sources reviewed; session usable; the IDOs and Sql Tables Forms closed clean and reopened fresh once each; in each, the FX_Orders criterion visible before F4 and zero data rows after it; the EXP-071 positive controls cited. Evidence: pre-F4 criterion and settled-result screenshots for both queries.
Dependency gate carried over from EXP-071 T1 (FX_HelloWorldProject01 and the three property classes with their EXP-070 values); nothing changed. Evidence: the EXP-071 screenshots cited.

Wizard route and header: New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance; IDO Name FX_Orders, Project FX_HelloWorldProject01, Alias fxords; Table Name read-only and empty. The Property Class lookup lists the three classes (or the single contingency unload is recorded with its reason and re-check). Evidence: header and lookup screenshots; unload count.

Exactly four properties in order with the specified classes, values and flags: FX_OrderNumber (Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key, Required); FX_CustomerID (Property Class FX_CustomerID, Required); FX_Item (Property Class FX_Item, Length overridden to 50, Required); FX_Count (Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount, Default Value 1); the inherited values and any SQL Column Data Type recorded. Evidence: per-row and four-row screenshots.
One Finish with its completion message; one No to Create Form; no Form created. Evidence: completion and prompt screenshots.

FX_Orders readback in the IDOs Form (project, table, alias, four properties, classes, effective values, Count default) and dbo.FX_Orders readback in SQL Columns (types, lengths, nullability, primary key FX_OrderNumber); the conditional check-in performed once or not needed. Evidence: IDO, SQL and check-in screenshots.
The IDOs and SQL Tables Forms each closed once more and reopened once more after creation; one exact-name query recovers each object matching its readback. Evidence: recovery screenshots.

The final EXP-071-R2 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-7, the complete action audit with exact counts (one Finish, one Create Form No, unloads 0 or 1 with reason, check-ins 0 or 1, Form close/reopen counts, recovery queries, zero changes to existing objects, zero strings created, re-login count), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.
